Benefit-risk scores and win statistics of simulated trials

Source: R/SimSelection.R
SimSelection.Rd

For each simulated trial, computes the posterior benefit-risk score of every cohort against target values and compares every other cohort with a reference cohort by the difference of these scores, optionally by the benefit-risk score relative to the reference cohort, and by generalized pairwise comparisons. The results are summarized by SelectionOC and CalibrateThreshold.

Usage

SimSelection(
  data,
  endpoints,
  criteria,
  reference,
  cohorts = NULL,
  criteria.ref = NULL,
  priority = NULL,
  threshold = NULL,
  scoring = c("gehan", "peron"),
  group = "group",
  sim = "sim",
  conf.level = 0.95,
  n.nodes = 200,
  scores = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Patient-level data of many simulated trials, for example from SimCohorts.

endpoints

An Endpoint object or a list of them.

criteria

Data frame of the components of the benefit-risk score against target values; see BenefitRisk.

reference

Name of the reference cohort.

cohorts

Names of the cohorts compared, including reference; by default all cohorts of data (in the order of the levels of a factor, otherwise in the order of appearance).

criteria.ref

Optional data frame of the components of the benefit-risk score relative to the reference cohort.

priority, threshold, scoring

Priority order, thresholds and scoring rule of the pairwise comparisons; see WinStat.

group, sim

Names of the columns of data with the cohort and the simulated trial.

conf.level

Confidence level of the lower bound of the net treatment benefit.

n.nodes

Number of Gauss-Legendre nodes for probabilities of differences.

scores

Logical: if TRUE, the posterior probabilities of the components are added to the output.

Value

A data frame of class SimSelection with one row per simulated trial and cohort and an attribute settings with the reference cohort, the scoring rule and the confidence level (see SimSelection-methods for print() and plot()). The statistics that compare a cohort with the reference cohort are NA in the rows of the reference cohort. With scores = TRUE, the posterior probabilities of the components are added after the columns below, in columns named S: (against target values) and ref: (relative to the reference cohort) followed by the label of the component. The columns are

sim

The simulated trial.

group

The cohort.

is_reference

Whether the cohort is the reference cohort.

br, adm

Benefit-risk score and admissibility against target values.

br_diff

Difference of br from that of the reference cohort.

br_ref, adm_ref

Benefit-risk score and admissibility relative to the reference cohort (only with criteria.ref).

p_win, p_loss, p_tie, ntb, ntb_se, ntb_lower, wr, wo

Proportions of pairs won, lost and tied against the reference cohort, net treatment benefit with its standard error and lower confidence bound, win ratio and win odds.

Details

The reference cohort is the one chosen when no other cohort is shown to be better, for example the cohort of the standard combination. The benefit-risk scores are computed as in BenefitRisk, with criteria for the scores against target values and criteria.ref for the scores relative to the reference cohort. The win statistics of a cohort are those of WinStat with the cohort as treatment and the reference cohort as control. Every simulated trial must contain patients of every cohort.

See also

SelectionOC, CalibrateThreshold

Examples

arms <- list(
  Cohort1 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 8, orr = 0.45, resp.cor = 0.4,
                                      death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 18),
  Cohort2 = CorOncoEndpoints::OncoArm(pfs.median = 6, orr = 0.30, resp.cor = 0.4,
                                      death.prop = 0.15, os.median = 15))
d <- SimCohorts(nsim = 20, n = c(40, 40), arms = arms, ae.rate = c(0.35, 0.20),
                cutoff = 24, a.time = c(0, 12), seed = 1)
eps <- list(Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),
            Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),
            Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),
            Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE))
crit <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "AE"), target = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.3),
                   time = c(NA, 6, NA))
crit_ref <- data.frame(endpoint = c("ORR", "PFS", "AE"),
                       measure = c("rate", "hr", "rate"),
                       target = c(0.1, 0.8, 0.1))
res <- SimSelection(d, eps, crit, reference = "Cohort2", criteria.ref = crit_ref)
head(res)
#> 6 rows of results of 3 simulated trials
#> Cohorts: Cohort1, Cohort2 (reference)
